options.title: LEGO Once Lost {fact1} in a Single Year
options.first_line: LEGO, the brick in your drawer, once lost about {fact1} in a single year.
options.first_frame: A heap of bright LEGO bricks, close and pushing in, the LEGO logo dropping in over them.

options.title: LEGO Almost Went Broke, and Kids Still Loved the Brick
options.first_line: LEGO almost went broke, while kids never stopped loving the brick.
options.first_frame: A heap of bright LEGO bricks, close and pushing in, a red stamp landing: 'nearly broke'.

options.title: LEGO Built Theme Parks. Then It Lost {fact1}
options.first_line: LEGO built theme parks and video games, then lost about {fact1} in one year.
options.first_frame: A heap of bright LEGO bricks with the LEGO logo, then a cut to a LEGO theme park train.

why: It names a brick everyone has touched and poses a paradox (beloved by kids yet nearly broke) that only the story answers, while A is just a big loss figure and C gives away the cause (theme parks and video games) in the title.
